fieldValues.title: An editor lists the packages it serves from its own site, and an agent can ask to install one but only the writer installs it
fieldValues.decision_question: Where does an editor find published packages, and who can install one into a document?
fieldValues.context: Problem: a writer whose essay needs something its packages don't have can't get it, and an agent can't help. Why it matters: each kind of writing will need its own types (SP-149, exercise fafd9091), which only works if a document can pick up a package. It also touches the rule that the writer decides what goes into their document. Options and consequences: see alternatives. Recommendation: this record's resolution. Action needed: ratify at a session. Urgency: srs-web#712 acts on it now and can be changed cheaply. Checked 2026-11-05 at srs-web 47b7e3d: release downloads send no CORS header, relay frames are answered synchronously (FrameHandler.handle), the core has parse_registry and check_package_requirements, and every published bundle has an empty description.
fieldValues.friction: The editor's errors tell the writer to install a package, with no way to do so. The owner on 2026-11-04: 'An essay should be able to find a list of published packages and install what is needed.'
fieldValues.alternatives_considered:
A. Do nothing: writers keep hitting errors they can't act on, and each kind of writing has to fit in the essay package.
B. Fetch from GitHub releases directly: no CORS header, so a browser can't.
C. A separate catalog host or a proxy: lets packages change between deploys, but adds a service with its own uptime and trust questions, for one publisher.
D. Serve from the site's own origin, generated from packages.lock.json, with the agent able only to ask. Chosen. Costs: publishing to writers takes a deploy.
E. As D, but the agent installs directly: quicker, but it would put definitions in a writer's document without their say, against the domain's rule that agents respond and don't write.
F. As D, with the agent's call waiting for the writer's answer: relay frames are synchronous, so it would need a change to the relay protocol, and a person can take minutes. The call returns at once and the agent reads the outcome from ui_packages instead.
fieldValues.key_requirements: A browser can fetch the list and bundles. A bundle is checked before it is installed. Nothing reaches a document without the writer's confirmation. The core decides what is satisfied. Packages nobody installs add nothing to the app's download.
fieldValues.decision_statement: An editor's list of published packages is an ext:registry catalog generated from its packages.lock.json and served, with the bundles, from its own origin. Install takes a catalog entry, never a URL, and checks the entry's sha256. A connected agent can read the list and ask; only the writer's confirmation on screen installs. A package not every document needs is not built into the app.
fieldValues.rationale: Own origin is the one option a browser can use today without a new service, and the lock already is the verified list of what we publish. Keeping the agent to asking keeps the writer in charge of their document: an installed package adds definitions they would then have to explain and keep. Generating the catalog in the ext:registry format means a later shared registry (RFC-047) can replace the source without changing the shape.
fieldValues.revisit_when: A publisher outside this programme needs to be listed, since that brings trust and signing and RFC-047 (srs#871). A writer needs a package between deploys. Wrong if writers confirm every agent request without reading it, so that confirmation stops meaning anything, or if a host with no writer present needs to install (srs-rust#1153).
fieldValues.next_steps: srs-web#712 builds this, recorded in ADR-031. A muDemocracy.org pull request publishes argument and governance so the list has a real second entry.
